snacs_adaptation_notes.txt:
SNACS v2.6 adaptation notes from authorized guidelines and four purchased reviews examples. Output each target as [scene role, lexical function], with p. prefixes. Scene role reflects the relation in context; function reflects what the marker conventionally expresses.

Genitives: possessive pronouns usually have p.Gestalt function, except canonical possession can have p.Possessor. Determine the pronoun referent's role relative to the head noun. 'my fusions' (the patient undergoing fusions) = p.Theme/p.Gestalt; 'my back' (back as body part of person) = p.Whole/p.Gestalt; 'my experience' (person experiencing) = p.Experiencer/p.Gestalt. Do not automatically assign p.Possessor simply because the form is possessive. Guideline §6.1: s-genitive functions are p.Gestalt or p.Possessor; scene roles can be participants, part-whole, social relations, etc. Of-genitives may use other functions such as p.Whole or p.Theme.

Quantity constructions: in 'a limited amount of time', of = p.QuantityItem/p.Gestalt. Guideline §4.3.4: for a measured item after 'amount/quantity/number' with a measure modifier, use this construal. Plain quantified nouns such as 'a lot of students' may be p.QuantityItem/p.QuantityItem; a specific definite item measured as a portion can be p.QuantityItem/p.Whole.

Purpose: 'recommend them for any custom lighting or Lighting Repair and Restoration' has for = p.Purpose/p.Purpose. The service/use being recommended is the intended purpose.

Time: 'Even after my fusions' has after = p.Time/p.Time; the surgery supplies the temporal reference for the later hurting. Preserve the lexical temporal function when it directly marks a time relation.

These are generalization aids, not labels for unseen examples. Check the actual governor and object in each new sentence.
